introPt: A traveller turns a day into an account someone wants to continue.
cenario: Chatting with the person behind the counter.

dialogo.pt: So, what did you do yesterday?

dialogo.es: Ieri sono andato a Firenze. Ho mangiato la bistecca alla fiorentina.
dialogo.pt: Yesterday I went to Florence. I ate the Florentine steak.

dialogo.es: Ah, quella vera! E dove, scusa?
dialogo.pt: Ah, the real one! And where, may I ask?

dialogo.es: Mi è piaciuto moltissimo. Domani andiamo a Siena. Lei c'è stato?
dialogo.pt: I liked it very much. Tomorrow we're going to Siena. Have you been?

perguntas.pergunta: Which verbs take sono in the past?
perguntas.explica: Sono andato, sono andata, siamo andati — the ending agrees with you.

perguntas.pergunta: Ho mangiato — why ho and not sono?
opcoes: Verbs that do something to a thing take ho, and never change ending
perguntas.explica: That difference is most of the grammar you need here.

opcoes: It pleased me — the thing is the subject
perguntas.explica: Which is why it changes with the thing, not with you.

perguntas.pergunta: Why name a low point in your account?
opcoes: Because liking everything reads as politeness rather than experience
perguntas.explica: It turns a report into a conversation.

opcoes: They are asking for the next level of detail
perguntas.explica: Answer with the specific, then hand the question back.
